title: Robust File and Exception Handling Practice
learningObjectives: Explain the main rules of robust file-processing workflow.
Identify the key C++ constructs used for robust file-processing workflow.
Apply robust file-processing workflow in a small program.
Recognize common failure cases and safety concerns.
Test a practical scenario and justify the chosen approach.

understand.concept: Reliable file processing combines checked opens and reads, line-based parsing, validation, a clear skip/abort policy, exception handling and RAII. For output, write to a temporary and verify before replacing final output when supported.
understand.whyItMatters: Real input and I/O fail unpredictably. Robust programs preserve valid data, explain rejected records and avoid claiming incomplete output is successful.

practise.guidedTask: Implement an importer that numbers lines, parses label and score, validates 0–100, collects valid rows and reports rejects. Test missing file, empty file, blank line, invalid score, extra field and valid row.
practise.independentTask: Build a grade report: malformed records are rejected but processing continues; missing input aborts; output is written to a temporary file and verified before considered ready. Include six tests.
hints: Define the record format and failure policy first.
Check open and read failures separately.
Parse into temporary values and validate before accumulation.
Report rejected rows with line numbers.
Check output after write and flush.
